evidence.curator_note: Book draws 2 arc(s); moves <1,3> are drawn, move <2> is an implicit hook required for electron balance (not drawn on the page): (i) the RIGHT fishhook has its tail under the C(6)=C(7) double bond - the ionized bond the bracket '+.' refers to - and its barb pointing up at the C(5)-C(6) bond = move 1 (odd electron into the forming pi bond); (ii) the LEFT fishhook has its tail on the cleaving C(4)-C(5) bond and its barb pointing left into the C(3)-C(4) bond region of the departing fragment = move 3 (the homolysis hook). NOT drawn: move 2, the second electron of the cleaving C(4)-C(5) bond entering the forming C(5)=C(6) pi bond. The two arcs sit in exactly the same places as in the crossed-out allo-Ocimene panel above; the panels differ only in the substrate. BARB PLACEMENT, stated honestly: the barb of arc (ii) lands in the C(3)-C(4) bond region rather than on C(4). One fishhook alone cannot raise C(3)-C(4) to a double bond (that needs two electrons and an additional, undrawn arc opening the exocyclic C(3)=C(10) pi bond), so this record deposits the electron on C(4), giving .CH2-C(=CH2)-CH=CH2. That radical is allylically delocalized, and its partner canonical form - odd electron on the exocyclic methylene C(10) with C(3)=C(4) double - is exactly what the barb pointing INTO the C(3)-C(4) bond depicts. This is the book's stated reason for the difference between the two panels: the cleaved C(4)-C(5) bond is allylic to the C(3)=C(10) methylene on one side and to C(6)=C(7) on the other, i.e. 'the cleaved bond is doubly allylic', so the channel is enhanced in myrcene while for allo-ocimene (where C(4) is sp2 and the departing radical would be vinylic) the arrow is crossed out. STRUCTURE AS DRAWN: CH2=CH-C(=CH2)-CH2-CH2-CH=C(CH3)2 (7-methyl-3-methyleneocta-1,6-diene, beta-myrcene); the drawing differs from the panel above only in that the substituent on C(3) is an exocyclic methylene (double vertical line) instead of a methyl, which makes C(3)-C(4) a single bond and C(4) an sp3 CH2. LOCALIZATION (convention B): the page draws the intact molecule in a bracket with '+.' outside, so this record localizes the ionized C(6)=C(7) pi bond as an odd electron on C(6) (where arc (i) starts) and the charge on C(7), the tertiary-cation end of the drawn product. RESONANCE (convention C): the product ion is printed as a delocalized allyl cation (an arc over C(5)-C(6)-C(7) with '+' underneath, no localized double bond); the form written here, CH2=CH-C(+)(CH3)2, is the one the arrows produce, its partner being (+)CH2-CH=C(CH3)2. MEASUREMENTS (convention F): the page prints NO m/z and NO intensity - the products are labelled only 'C5H7.' and a structure carrying '+' - so both products are detected=false, no relative_intensity is recorded, and the 69.0699 in peak_assignments is the curator-computed monoisotopic m/z of C5H9+ (status 'inferred'), not a measured value. The prose calls this ion abundant only indirectly, via the homosqualene (M-83)+ discussion that follows.

No MOD rule carries equation id 9.4 or any 9.x id (rule_index.json 'by_equation' has no chapter-9 key), so the cross-link is to the Equation 4.15 allylic-cleavage family the page cites for this reaction type. Verified against the DFS, not asserted: IMS_4_15_1_1 '[C]1[C]2[C+.]3[C]4>>[C.]1.[C]2{=}[C]3[C+]4' and IMS_4_15_1_2 '[C]1[C]2[C]3[C+.]4>>[C.]1.[C]2{=}[C]3[C+]4' cleave C1-C2 and raise C2-C3 from single to double, the cleaved bond being incident to the pi-forming atom C2 - the same pair of bond changes as encoded here (cleave C(4)-C(5), form C(5)=C(6)) - and release the departing fragment as [C.], matching C5H7; IMS_4_15_2_2 is the same net reaction written in the product ion's partner canonical form. MISMATCH, RDKit-tested: their left pattern requires ONE carbon carrying both the charge and the odd electron ([C+.]); this record's localized precursor has no such atom, so the 4-carbon-chain search for it returns 0 matches, while the motif actually present (radical-C(6) then cation-C(7)) matches at maps (4,5,6,7), i.e. on the cleaved bond and the forming pi bond. Defects in the 8-carbon variants, measured by importing src/data_generation/rules in the container: the conservation guardrail drops IMS_4_15_3_1 and IMS_4_15_2_1 with 'spin 1->0', and IMS_4_15_3_2 survives but its product '[C.]1.[C+]2[C]3[C]4[C]5[C]6[C]7[C]8' contains no new double bond, so it does not describe this cleavage. Finally, no 4.15 DFS requires a C=C anywhere, so the rule set cannot express what Equation 9.4 is actually about - the contrast between a vinylic (retarded, panel a) and a doubly allylic (enhanced, panel b) cleaved bond; a rule that fires identically on both panels reproduces neither statement. MS conditions: the page states none; 70 eV EI is the book's standard for these hydrocarbon spectra.
